tagline: Across the San Luis Valley, oldest parish to oldest town.
intro: From Cumbres Pass the byway comes down to Antonito, where the Cumbres & Toltec Scenic Railroad keeps its Colorado terminus, and sets out across the San Luis Valley, a high basin between the Sangre de Cristos and the San Juans that averages 7,664 feet. It passes Conejos and Manassa, crosses to San Luis and Fort Garland, and swings north toward the Great Sand Dunes before it finishes at Alamosa, 129 miles in all.

The dunes, the tallest in North America at up to 750 feet, are more than a thousand miles from the nearest ocean beach. Wind carried the sand off an old lakebed and piled it against a low curve in the Sangre de Cristo Range.

moments.title: Conejos
moments.text: Our Lady of Guadalupe, founded in 1858 and built by Spanish colonists from Taos, was the first Roman Catholic parish in present-day Colorado, and Conejos is the state's last unincorporated county seat.

moments.title: San Luis
moments.text: Settlers from the Taos Valley took possession here in April 1851 and dedicated their church that June, and the town has been occupied ever since, longer than any other in Colorado.

moments.title: Fort Garland
moments.text: Kit Carson commanded the post and lived with his wife in the adobe Commandant's Quarters, and the Buffalo Soldiers of the Ninth Cavalry were stationed here from 1876 to 1879.
